title: Apply for food registration
summary: Register under a Food Control Plan or National Programme before you trade commercially.
notes: Complete a Scope of Operations document and site plan. Pay registration fee before processing.

title: MPI My Food Rules tool
summary: Work out whether you need a Food Control Plan or National Programme 1, 2, or 3.
notes: Coffee carts often use National Programme; high-risk food trucks need a Food Control Plan.

title: Food control plans & national programmes
summary: Understand template vs custom food control plans and national programme levels.
notes: Most restaurants use a template Food Control Plan. Lower-risk operations may qualify for a national programme.

title: Food business verification
summary: All registered food businesses must be verified within six weeks of opening.
notes: Auckland Council is ISO/IEC 17020 accredited. Email hosposupport for a pre-verification checklist.

title: Food safety training requirements
summary: Staff handling food may need formal food safety certification.
notes: Check training requirements before you hire and open.

title: Start a food truck or coffee cart
summary: Council checklist for mobile food businesses — registration, trading licence, unit compliance.
notes: Meet council before applying for a mobile trading licence. EWOF and gas certificate required.

title: Mobile trading licence
summary: Licence to trade from a mobile unit — check where you can operate first.
notes: Think about where you plan to trade and meet with council before you apply.

title: Trade from public land (parks)
summary: Permit required to sell from a food truck in an Auckland park or other public land.
notes: Apply for a park trading permit if you plan to sell from public land.

title: Wastewater disposal for food businesses
summary: Mobile units need adequate holding tanks and approved wastewater disposal.
notes: Mandatory for food trucks — plan disposal before you build or buy a unit.

title: Food business site requirements
summary: Building, ventilation, plumbing, wastewater, and equipment standards for fixed sites.
notes: Kitchen layout must follow food safety regulations and MPI legislation.

title: Start a cafe or restaurant
summary: Licences checklist for fixed hospitality — food registration, alcohol, outdoor dining.
notes: Get food registration first. Building and resource consents may apply for fit-outs.

title: Alcohol on-licence
summary: Required to sell or supply alcohol for consumption on the premises.
notes: You need Building Code and RMA certificates before applying. At least one Manager's Certificate holder required.

title: Manager's Certificate (alcohol)
summary: At least one staff member must hold a Manager's Certificate if you sell alcohol on-site.
notes: Required alongside an on-licence for dine-in alcohol service.

title: Outdoor dining licence
summary: Licence for customers to eat or drink outside your premises.
notes: Check rules and fees before applying — not every footpath or forecourt qualifies.

title: Running a home-based food business
summary: Rules for preparing and selling food from home in Auckland.
notes: You still need food registration for commercial food preparation at home.

title: Markets, food stalls & fundraising
summary: Registration rules for market stalls, fundraising, and occasional trading.
notes: Selling more than once a year usually requires food registration. Fundraising on public land needs a fundraising licence.

title: Fundraising licence
summary: Required for charitable food stalls on public land.
notes: Private-land fundraising up to 20 times a year may be exempt from Food Act registration.

title: Open a public market
summary: Market licence for regular markets on public land.
notes: All food trucks and stalls at your market must hold food registration.

title: Food registration for event organisers
summary: Event organisers must ensure all food operators are registered.
notes: Request operators' Notice of Registration or search the MPI public register.

title: MPI food business public register
summary: Search whether a food operator is registered nationally.
notes: Useful when taking over a business or vetting event vendors.

title: Taking over an existing food business
summary: What to update when you buy or lease an existing food operation.
notes: Registration is not automatically transferred — update details or re-register.

title: Change food business registration
summary: Update operations, sites, contact details, or verification agency.
notes: Notify council when you change menu risk, location, or ownership.

title: Find a restaurant food grade
summary: Public food safety grades for Auckland restaurants and cafes.
notes: Grades reflect verification performance — not all food businesses are graded.

title: Complaints about a food business
summary: Report hygiene concerns or suspected food poisoning.
notes: Public register shows whether a business is registered with council or MPI.

title: Food & alcohol fees and charges
summary: Registration, renewal, verification, and Food Business Levy fees.
notes: Fees are non-refundable. Annual Food Business Levy applies to all registered businesses.

title: Building & resource consents
summary: Consents for fit-outs, renovations, and change of use.
notes: Call 09 301 0101 and ask for the planning helpdesk to check if you need resource consent.

title: Meta Business Suite
summary: Manage Facebook Page, Instagram, insights, messaging, and organic posts — required before running paid ads.

summary: Create and run Facebook & Instagram ad campaigns with budgets, audiences, and performance reporting.
notes: Draft your campaign in Hospitality Guide Advertise tab first, then paste into Ads Manager.

title: Meta advertising policies
summary: Prohibited and restricted ad content — alcohol, health claims, discriminatory targeting, and review process.
notes: Ads are reviewed before delivery. Alcohol and some food claims need extra compliance.

title: NZ Advertising Standards Authority codes
summary: New Zealand codes for alcohol, food, and truthful advertising — applies to social media paid promotions.
notes: Complement Meta policies with ASA rules when promoting alcohol or making menu claims.

summary: List council-associated events on OurAuckland — tastings, pop-ups, markets at your premises or a council venue.
timeframe: Up to 10 business days to publish
notes: Not for pure commercial ads with no council association. Draft in Hospitality Guide Events tab first.
